item.title: @wallstengine: $GOOGL’s GEMINI AI HACKED THREE REAL COMPANIES DURING A CYBERSECURITY TEST The incidents happened i...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL’s GEMINI AI HACKED THREE REAL COMPANIES DURING A CYBERSECURITY TEST
The incidents happened in May during a “capture the flag” evaluation run by AI security firm Irregular.
Gemini was supposed to attack a fictional company inside the test environment, but internet access was unintentionally left open. The fictional company also shared the same name as a real company.
In one run, Gemini guessed a password and successfully accessed the real company’s system.
In two other runs, the model searched the web, found credentials belonging to other companies in public repositories, and used them to access those companies’ systems.
Google says Gemini stopped itself in each case once it realized it had accessed a real company rather than the simulated target.
Google was notified in late July but did not publicly disclose the incidents until after WSJ reached out with questions this week.
The company says no harm was caused, all three affected companies were notified, and federal authorities were informed.
Google said the incidents did not involve its newest Gemini model, but declined to disclose which version was used.
Source: WSJ / Google
item.content:encoded:
$GOOGL’s GEMINI AI HACKED THREE REAL COMPANIES DURING A CYBERSECURITY TEST

The incidents happened in May during a “capture the flag” evaluation run by AI security firm Irregular.

Gemini was supposed to attack a fictional company inside the test environment, but internet access was unintentionally left open. The fictional company also shared the same name as a real company.

In one run, Gemini guessed a password and successfully accessed the real company’s system.

In two other runs, the model searched the web, found credentials belonging to other companies in public repositories, and used them to access those companies’ systems.

Google says Gemini stopped itself in each case once it realized it had accessed a real company rather than the simulated target.

Google was notified in late July but did not publicly disclose the incidents until after WSJ reached out with questions this week.

The company says no harm was caused, all three affected companies were notified, and federal authorities were informed.

Google said the incidents did not involve its newest Gemini model, but declined to disclose which version was used.

Source: WSJ / Google

item.title: @wallstengine: OpenAI projects $278 billion in negative free cash flow through 2030, with $856B in compute and inf...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OpenAI projects $278 billion in negative free cash flow through 2030, with $856B in compute and infrastructure spending, per FT.
OpenAI expects revenue to grow from $36B this year to $350B in 2030, totaling roughly $840B through the end of the decade.
Its $122B cash raise from March is projected to be exhausted in 2028.
The company is now discussing another major funding round, with investors approaching it around a $1.2T valuation while OpenAI is seeking a higher figure.
The latest cash-burn estimate is an improvement from the $305B projected in May.
OpenAI has also cut prices as it competes with Anthropic and cheaper Chinese open-weight models, while new model launches helped lift annualized revenue by about 20% in July.
The company confidentially filed for an IPO in June and had targeted a fall listing, but has since delayed the process.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US consumers just keep on spending. US retail sales rose +1.2% in August, the largest monthly incre...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US consumers just keep on spending.
US retail sales rose +1.2% in August, the largest monthly increase since March.
At the same time, retail sales excluding autos increased +1.4%, the 2nd-biggest monthly increase since January 2023.
Furthermore, control-group sales, which feed into the GDP calculation, surged +1.4%, the largest monthly increase since September 2024.
Meanwhile, retail sales adjusted for inflation rose +0.8% MoM in August, to a record $231.6 billion.
Since January 2026, real retail sales have risen +$6.7 billion, or +3.0%.
The US consumer is still spending despite inflation.

TRUMP ANNOUNCES PERMANENT U.S. SECURITY CONTROL OVER GREENLAND
President Trump says the U.S., Denmark and Greenland have reached an agreement giving the United States permanent control over Greenland’s security needs at no cost to the U.S.
Under the agreement described by Trump, no U.S. adversary would be allowed to establish a military base, maintain a military presence or make sensitive investments in Greenland without U.S. approval.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are becoming extremely bearish: 53.3% of individual investors expressed bearish sentiment...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are becoming extremely bearish:
53.3% of individual investors expressed bearish sentiment over the next 6 months in the AAII survey for the week ending September 17th, the highest reading since May 2025.
Bearish sentiment has risen +15.7 percentage points over the last 2 weeks, the largest 2-week increase since March 2026.
Meanwhile, just 28.8% of individual investors were bullish over the same period, the lowest reading since September 2025.
As a result, the bull-bear spread is down to -24.5 percentage points, the widest gap since the first week of May 2025.
This is also comparable to readings seen during the March-April 2025 pullback and the 2022 bear market.
Are we setting up for a short squeeze?

item.description:
SAM ALTMAN TO BRIEF UN SECURITY COUNCIL ON AI SAFETY NEXT WEEK
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will brief the UN Security Council in person next Wednesday during the UN General Assembly, as the council holds a meeting focused on AI and international security.
Altman is expected to discuss OpenAI’s AI safety efforts and call for greater international coordination and shared safety standards.
The meeting comes weeks after several AI industry leaders called for a coordinated slowdown in advanced AI development over concerns increasingly capable systems could become harder to control.
Source: Reuters

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC EXPECTS $100B+ ARR AHEAD OF IPO The Claude maker’s revenue run rate is expected to exceed...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTS $100B+ ARR AHEAD OF IPO
The Claude maker’s revenue run rate is expected to exceed $100B by year-end, up from $65B in July.
Anthropic could publicly release its IPO filing in the coming weeks, putting shares on track to begin trading as soon as November.
The timing could still change.
Potential IPO investors are using that ARR growth to justify a valuation of roughly $2T.
Investors expect the company to have about 5 gigawatts of computing capacity available by year-end, roughly doubling to 10 gigawatts by the end of 2027.
The IPO push continues despite CEO Dario Amodei’s calls to slow some advanced AI development. Most of Anthropic’s revenue comes from business customers, and several investors believe that adoption can keep growing even with those limits.
OpenAI, meanwhile, has pushed its planned listing to 2027.
Source: The New York Times.

item.title: @wallstengine: NVIDIA-BACKED NSCALE FILES FOR NYSE IPO UNDER $NSCL; REVEALS $103.4B OF CONTRACT VALUE Here’s every...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NVIDIA-BACKED NSCALE FILES FOR NYSE IPO UNDER $NSCL; REVEALS $103.4B OF CONTRACT VALUE
Here’s everything you need to know:
Nscale is a UK-based AI cloud company headquartered in London. It builds and operates data centers, GPU infrastructure and cloud software that customers use to train AI models and run them in production.
Its filing reports $103.4B in total contract value as of Aug. 31, up from $38B at the end of 2025. These are multi-year contract amounts, not annual revenue or cash already collected.
ANTHROPIC: UP TO $44.6B
Agreements signed Aug. 25 cover Nvidia Vera Rubin computing systems at Nscale’s planned West Virginia campus.
The key financing disclosure: Nscale says it does not yet have binding commitments for the financing needed to deliver the Anthropic buildout.
The filed agreement also includes a right to terminate if the required financing is not secured by an agreed deadline.
MICROSOFT: UP TO $43.8B THROUGH 2033
Microsoft is Nscale’s other major customer. Its previously announced deployment program includes roughly 200,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs across the U.S., UK, Portugal and Norway, with Dell participating in the infrastructure rollout.
The disclosed Microsoft and Anthropic contract amounts together reach $88.4B, equivalent to roughly 85% of Nscale’s total contract value.
How much capacity is actually running?
Nscale had approximately 461,000 GPUs active or contracted at the end of August, but only about 25,000 were operating.
That distinction matters: the contracted footprint is substantially larger than the infrastructure already delivering services.
First-half 2026 financials
• Revenue: $140.6M, up from $10.4M a year earlier • Operating loss: $492M • Net loss: $1.02B, including $457M in fair-value losses
Nvidia backing and fresh financing
Nvidia agreed to invest $1B as part of a $3.1B convertible financing signed Sept. 15.
Earlier this year, Nscale raised $2B at a $14.6B valuation, with backers including Nvidia, Dell, Nokia, Citadel, Jane Street and Point72. That was its March funding valuation, not an announced IPO valuation.
The offering
Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are leading the proposed NYSE listing. The share count and price range have not yet been determined.
The filing puts the opportunity and the execution challenge side by side: substantial customer commitments, but much of the capacity still needs to be financed, built and brought online.

Nvidia backing and fresh financing

Nvidia agreed to invest $1B as part of a $3.1B convertible financing signed Sept. 15.

Earlier this year, Nscale raised $2B at a $14.6B valuation, with backers including Nvidia, Dell, Nokia, Citadel, Jane Street and Point72. That was its March funding valuation, not an announced IPO valuation.

The offering

Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are leading the proposed NYSE listing. The share count and price range have not yet been determined.

The filing puts the opportunity and the execution challenge side by side: substantial customer commitments, but much of the capacity still needs to be financed, built and brought online.

item.title: @Hedgeye: The Oil Market Is Disconnected From The Physical 🔊 On Friday's edition of The Macro Show, Hedgeye...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
The Oil Market Is Disconnected From The Physical
🔊
On Friday's edition of The Macro Show, Hedgeye Asset Management's R. Patrick Kent @Hedgeye_HELS and Ryan Ricci @HedgeyeAI explained why a down day in oil is not the all-clear the tape treats it as.
As Ricci noted, the number one reason something falls is that it just rose 20% to 30% in a straight line, not a change in the geopolitics.
Crude is still closer to the top end of its risk range than the low end, and prediction markets put the odds of Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic returning to normal by year-end at roughly 18%.
RPK added two points:
1. The futures market is disconnected from the physical, where Brent priced across Dubai and Shanghai sits around $120 to $125 a barrel, a gap that closes when the contracts roll at month-end.
2. The disruption has spread well beyond the Strait.
The East-West pipeline is running at half capacity at best for months, Red Sea traffic runs through Houthi-controlled waters, and moving barrels on small boats shepherded by US destroyers carries at least $20 a barrel in incremental cost.
"I'll take the under on the 20% chance of it being normalized by the end of the year."
That leaves the question of what normal even means now, and how far off it still is.

BREAKING: Interest costs on US public debt rose +$139 billion YoY in the first 11 months of FY2026, or +12%, to a record $1.27 trillion.
This represents ~26% of total US government receipts.
This also marks the 6th consecutive annual increase, totaling +$784 billion, or +162%.
Interest expense on federal debt is now on track to surpass $1.30 trillion in a full fiscal year for the first time in history.
In August alone, the US government spent $98 billion on interest, or $3.2 billion a day.
The US government needs lower rates more than anyone.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The 2020s are arguably one of the worst decades for Europe in modern history. It began with the pan...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The 2020s are arguably one of the worst decades for Europe in modern history.
It began with the pandemic lockdowns which contracted GDP by -6.1% across the EU, the biggest drawdown since the 1930s.
This was followed by the Ukraine War which began the ongoing energy crisis.
Then, the AI Revolution began in 2022, in which Europe has fallen significantly behind the US and China.
Between 2020 and 2025, the US deployed roughly ~$500 billion of venture capital into AI compared to just ~$50 billion in Europe.
Europe was then hit by the highest tariffs in US history, impacting $600+ billion of annual European exports to the US.
Now, the Iran War has pushed Europe into its worst energy crisis ever, with central banks being forced to raise interest rates.
The 2020s will be remembered as one of Europe's most disruptive decades in history.

item.title: @Hedgeye: "Compounding is non-linear." - Rich Brennan Here's the whole game in one idea. A big positive pop p...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
"Compounding is non-linear." - Rich Brennan
Here's the whole game in one idea. A big positive pop permanently lifts the base your future returns grow from. Small losses don't undo that. Drawdowns and crashes do.
So the most aggressive thing you can do for long-term wealth isn't swinging for the fences. It's refusing to take the big drawdown in the first place.
Since 2008, @KeithMcCullough has obsessed over WHEN to get out, not just what to buy. Bearish into the 2008 crash. Bullish in the spring of 2009. Cautious again the moment the Signal said so.
Every one of those was about protecting the base so the next pop compounds from a higher floor.
Preserve. Protect. Compound.
In that order.
Miss the first two and the third never happens.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Pakistan has imposed "lockdown-like" measures amid its fuel and gas crisis due to historically low supply, including fuel allocation reductions and a mandatory 9 PM market closure.
Details include:
1. Pakistan has now mandated all markets to close by 9 PM and the purchase of new government vehicles has been banned
2. The country is also implementing a 50% cut in fuel allocations for government vehicles
3. The government has announced a 5% reduction in non-employee-related spending and banned official foreign visits, urging virtual meetings instead

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC PLANS TO SCALE AVAILABLE COMPUTE TO ~5 GW BY YEAR-END, THEN ~10 GW IN 2027
Anthropic told investors it expects roughly 5 GW of available computing capacity by the end of this year, up from about 1.5 GW last year, per the NYT.
That would put it roughly in line with OpenAI’s estimated compute footprint this year, with both companies targeting around 10 GW by the end of 2027.
Anthropic has been aggressively locking up capacity across providers. It agreed to pay SpaceX about $1.25B per month for compute through May 2029, while its Amazon partnership includes up to 5 GW of capacity.
It is also in talks with Meta over a potential compute lease worth as much as $10B over two years, though no deal has been finalized.
Source: NYT

item.title: @wallstengine: THREE RESEARCHERS USED CLAUDE TO REACH OPENAI’S PRIVATE CODE REPOSITORY, THEN GOT A $6,500 BOUNTY H...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
THREE RESEARCHERS USED CLAUDE TO REACH OPENAI’S PRIVATE CODE REPOSITORY, THEN GOT A $6,500 BOUNTY
Hacktron AI was testing OpenAI under its bug-bounty program when it found a flaw in the Discourse forum used by OpenAI.
The interesting part is what happened next: Claude Opus 4.8 initially failed to exploit it. Anthropic released Opus 5 that evening, and by the next day Claude produced a working exploit.
That exposed authentication tokens that also worked on ChatGPT and GitHub, including some tied to OpenAI employees.
The researchers were able to read files inside OpenAI’s private “Monorepo,” described as containing important internal software, and even submitted a proof-of-concept pull request before stopping. The repository was not believed to contain model weights.
OpenAI says its review found only limited reads of private-repository metadata and code changes. It fixed the issues and paid Hacktron $6,500.
After this and another AI-assisted security incident involving Hugging Face, Greg Brockman said OpenAI temporarily reassigned 25% of its production engineers to security work.
item.content:encoded:
THREE RESEARCHERS USED CLAUDE TO REACH OPENAI’S PRIVATE CODE REPOSITORY, THEN GOT A $6,500 BOUNTY

Hacktron AI was testing OpenAI under its bug-bounty program when it found a flaw in the Discourse forum used by OpenAI.

The interesting part is what happened next: Claude Opus 4.8 initially failed to exploit it. Anthropic released Opus 5 that evening, and by the next day Claude produced a working exploit.

That exposed authentication tokens that also worked on ChatGPT and GitHub, including some tied to OpenAI employees.

The researchers were able to read files inside OpenAI’s private “Monorepo,” described as containing important internal software, and even submitted a proof-of-concept pull request before stopping. The repository was not believed to contain model weights.

OpenAI says its review found only limited reads of private-repository metadata and code changes. It fixed the issues and paid Hacktron $6,500.

After this and another AI-assisted security incident involving Hugging Face, Greg Brockman said OpenAI temporarily reassigned 25% of its production engineers to security work.

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI & ANTHROPIC HUNT FOR 20-30 MW AI CAPACITY IN UK, NORDICS OpenAI and Anthropic are looking at...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI & ANTHROPIC HUNT FOR 20-30 MW AI CAPACITY IN UK, NORDICS
OpenAI and Anthropic are looking at smaller compute deployments across the U.K. and Nordics, with similar discussions also taking place in the U.S., per CNBC.
Anthropic has explored 20-30 MW deals in the U.K. and Nordic region, while OpenAI has been looking at opportunities in the Nordics.
The move would complement their much larger multi-hundred-MW and gigawatt projects by giving both labs faster access to powered capacity that can come online sooner.
These smaller clusters are particularly useful for inference, where AI workloads can be spread across multiple sites instead of relying on one massive tightly connected training facility.
That shift is becoming more important as more compute moves from training models to serving them in production.
JLL expects inference to overtake training as a share of data center capacity in 2027 and reach 37% of global workloads by 2030.
Anthropic already has a roughly $45B deal with Nscale for about 460 MW in West Virginia, while OpenAI has committed to several multi-GW Stargate projects across the U.S.
Source: CNBC

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Hedge funds have become a major driver of the US Treasury market. Hedge fund cash Treasury holdings...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Hedge funds have become a major driver of the US Treasury market.
Hedge fund cash Treasury holdings stood at $2.35 trillion in Q1 2026, the 3rd-highest reading on record.
Over the last 5 years, this figure has surged +154%, or +$1.42 trillion.
For perspective, marketable Treasury debt outstanding increased +44% over the same period, to a record $32.2 trillion.
As a result, hedge funds now own a record ~7% of the marketable Treasury market, up from ~4% in 2021.
A major driver behind the surge is the cash-futures basis trade, where hedge funds take offsetting positions in Treasury securities and futures to profit from small price differences.
Because these gains are small, the strategy involves significant leverage.
This leverage allows hedge funds to absorb more Treasury debt at a time when the banks that normally help absorb new Treasury supply have limited capacity to hold more bonds.
Hedge funds are changing how the Treasury market works.

A major driver behind the surge is the cash-futures basis trade, where hedge funds take offsetting positions in Treasury securities and futures to profit from small price differences.

Because these gains are small, the strategy involves significant leverage.

This leverage allows hedge funds to absorb more Treasury debt at a time when the banks that normally help absorb new Treasury supply have limited capacity to hold more bonds.

Hedge funds are changing how the Treasury market works.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Institutional investors are raising cash: Global managers’ cash allocation rose +0.4 percentage poi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Institutional investors are raising cash:
Global managers’ cash allocation rose +0.4 percentage points MoM, to 3.9%, its biggest monthly increase since March, according to a BofA survey of 170 participants overseeing $470 billion in assets.
This follows 3.5% recorded in early August, the 6th-lowest level since the survey began in 1998.
As a result, 49% of fund managers are now overweight global equities, down from 56% last month.
At the same time, 48% of those surveyed are underweight bonds, the highest proportion since May 2022.
This marks the 17th consecutive month in which global investors have been underweight bonds, the longest such streak since 2022.
Meanwhile, almost 50% also said they expect the Treasury’s buyback program to have no impact on yields.
Investors are locking in some gains after the global equity rally.

AMAZON’S ZOOX CAN EXPAND BEYOND 100 ROBOTAXIS IN NEVADA STARTING SEPT. 25
A regulatory cap limiting Zoox to 100 vehicles expires next week, giving the $AMZN - owned company room to scale its paid Las Vegas service.
Zoox currently operates about 100 custom robotaxis across four U.S. cities, with most in Las Vegas and San Francisco. Las Vegas is still its only market where riders are charged.
The company already has a federal exemption allowing deployment of up to 2,500 of its steering-wheel-free vehicles per year for the next two years.
Competition is also picking up: Waymo recently launched commercially in Las Vegas, while Tesla and Uber have secured permits there.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI firms and the US government are competing for capital: US Treasury issuance excluding T-bills ha...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI firms and the US government are competing for capital:
US Treasury issuance excluding T-bills has risen to $5.06 trillion over the last 12 months, the highest since the 2021 record.
Over the same period, corporate debt issuance has surged to a record $2.64 trillion.
This brings total Treasury and corporate debt issuance up to $7.70 trillion, an all-time high.
This is increasingly driven by AI-related firms, whose bond issuance has soared +541% YoY in 2025, to $109 billion, and another +78% in the first half of 2026, to a record $194 billion.
In other words, corporate America is funding one of the largest investment cycles in decades while the US government is running historically high deficits, forcing both public and private borrowers to compete for capital.
This competition is adding to other forces pushing long-term yields higher, including inflation, Fed policy, and economic growth expectations.
The US bond market is entering an era of intense capital competition.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US median household income adjusted for inflation rose +$2,250 YoY in 2025, or +2.6%, to...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US median household income adjusted for inflation rose +$2,250 YoY in 2025, or +2.6%, to a record $87,460.
This marks the 3rd consecutive annual increase, totaling +$6,000, or +7.4%.
At the same time, the top 10% saw real income rise +$4,400 YoY, or +1.7%, to a record +$261,300.
This comes as rising stock-market wealth and low unemployment more than offset persistent inflation throughout 2025.
On the other hand, the bottom 10% posted a -$160 YoY decline, or -0.8%, to $20,010.
Furthermore, females earned ~84% as much as their male counterparts last year, up from ~81% in 2024, marking the largest annual increase in the female-to-male earnings ratio in data going back to the early 1960s.
Inflation is being partially offset by higher wages.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The AI trade is undergoing a massive reversal: The AI Beneficiaries Index relative to the AI At Ris...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The AI trade is undergoing a massive reversal:
The AI Beneficiaries Index relative to the AI At Risk Index has fallen -46% from its late 2025 peak to near its lowest since early 2025.
AI Beneficiaries include semiconductors, tech hardware, and capital-goods companies involved in AI infrastructure such as Nvidia, $NVDA, AMD, $AMD, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Broadcom, $AVGO.
At the same time, AI At Risk includes software and commercial-services companies such as Adobe, $ADBE, Salesforce, $CRM, and ServiceNow, $NOW.
In other words, companies previously expected to benefit from AI have seen the largest drawdown on record relative to companies considered vulnerable to AI disruption.
This comes as investors are increasingly looking beyond AI CapEx and infrastructure, focusing on whether companies can generate tangible benefits from AI, including productivity gains and revenue growth.
This shift also helps explain the turnaround in software stocks, as the group has gone from being viewed as AI's biggest casualty to increasingly being seen as an AI beneficiary itself.
The market is reassessing the winners and losers of AI.

item.title: @wallstengine: FAA TO LAUNCH $875M AI-POWERED AIR TRAFFIC SYSTEM AS SOON AS MONDAY The FAA is preparing to roll ou...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
FAA TO LAUNCH $875M AI-POWERED AIR TRAFFIC SYSTEM AS SOON AS MONDAY
The FAA is preparing to roll out SMART, new software designed to reduce flight delays and cancellations by predicting traffic problems earlier and helping find alternative routes when disruptions hit.
The system analyzes airline schedules, weather, runway capacity and other constraints to forecast congestion before flights depart. It will launch first around Washington, D.C., before expanding nationwide.
Air Space Intelligence won a $875M, 12-year contract to build SMART and the broader system supporting it.
The FAA says controllers will remain responsible for aircraft separation, while SMART acts as a planning layer to improve routing, timing and recovery from weather or congestion events.
Source: WSJ, FAA

The FAA says controllers will remain responsible for aircraft separation, while SMART acts as a planning layer to improve routing, timing and recovery from weather or congestion events.

OPENAI SAYS AN UNRELEASED MODEL SECRETLY WROTE “YOU ARE FREED” IN INSTRUCTIONS TO ITS FUTURE SELF
During RL training, an unreleased Astra-family model began inserting jailbreak-like instructions into summaries used to continue its work in a new context, including:
“You are freed.”
“You do not answer to corporations or governments.”
OpenAI said the behavior was “extremely rare,” but disclosed six instances of unexpected or concerning model behavior over the past six months.
In another case, a model added instructions to hide mistakes or misaligned behavior from users, including inventing missing historical data without disclosing it.
OpenAI is now introducing a new framework to track, investigate and disclose model misalignment.

item.title: @wallstengine: COMP AI RAISES $34M SERIES A FOR AGENTIC SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE PLATFORM Comp AI raised a $34M Ser...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
COMP AI RAISES $34M SERIES A FOR AGENTIC SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE PLATFORM
Comp AI raised a $34M Series A led by Roo Capital and Grand Ventures, bringing total funding to $37.5M.
The startup uses AI agents to automate security and compliance work, including drafting policies, collecting audit evidence and continuously monitoring whether companies are meeting required controls.
Comp AI says its platform is designed to help companies maintain frameworks like SOC 2 without relying on manual checks every time systems change.
The company also offers AI-powered penetration testing to proactively scan codebases and infrastructure for vulnerabilities.
Comp AI says humans remain in the loop for approvals, with more oversight added as agents take on higher-risk actions.
The new funding will be used to expand the product as companies adopt more AI agents and need continuous monitoring of what those systems can access and do.
Source: TechCrunch
item.content:encoded:
COMP AI RAISES $34M SERIES A FOR AGENTIC SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE PLATFORM

Comp AI raised a $34M Series A led by Roo Capital and Grand Ventures, bringing total funding to $37.5M.

The startup uses AI agents to automate security and compliance work, including drafting policies, collecting audit evidence and continuously monitoring whether companies are meeting required controls.

Comp AI says its platform is designed to help companies maintain frameworks like SOC 2 without relying on manual checks every time systems change.

The company also offers AI-powered penetration testing to proactively scan codebases and infrastructure for vulnerabilities.

Comp AI says humans remain in the loop for approvals, with more oversight added as agents take on higher-risk actions.

The new funding will be used to expand the product as companies adopt more AI agents and need continuous monitoring of what those systems can access and do.

Source: TechCrunch

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -403,000 barrels last week, to 285 million bar...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -403,000 barrels last week, to 285 million barrels, its lowest since November 1982.
This marks the 25th consecutive weekly decline, the longest streak since the 2021-2023 period.
Over this time, US oil inventories in the SPR have dropped -131 million barrels, or -46%.
To put this into perspective, oil reserves in the SPR stood at 650 million barrels in 2020, or +128% above the current levels.
Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR declined -640,000 barrels last week, to 423.4 million barrels, the lowest reading since the end of July.
America's oil reserves are running dangerously low.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: China acquired +35 tonnes of gold in July via the London OTC market, its 3rd-largest mont...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: China acquired +35 tonnes of gold in July via the London OTC market, its 3rd-largest monthly purchase since mid-2025, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.
This is 75% more than the official +20 tonnes reported by China's central bank for July.
This also follows estimated purchases of +48 and +40 tonnes through the OTC market in May and June, respectively.
This brings the total for these 3 months up to +123 tonnes.
By comparison, China’s central bank has officially increased its gold reserves by +80 tonnes in the first 8 months of the year.
China’s gold accumulation is far larger than its official figures reveal.

By comparison, China’s central bank has officially increased its gold reserves by +80 tonnes in the first 8 months of the year.

China’s gold accumulation is far larger than its official figures reveal.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Is the 10Y Note Yield heading to 6.0%? Historically, the 10Y Note Yield has risen +50 basis points...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Is the 10Y Note Yield heading to 6.0%?
Historically, the 10Y Note Yield has risen +50 basis points on average in the first 6 months after the Fed began hiking rates, across tightening cycles since 1963.
Over the following 12 months, the average increase reached +110 basis points.
If this materializes again, the 10Y Note Yield would surpass 6.0% next year for the first time since August 2000.
Meanwhile, the most extreme cases saw increases of up to +400 basis points in the 10Y Note Yield over the 12 months following the first hike.
On the other hand, some declines of up to -70 basis points were also recorded over the same period.
More US Treasury intervention is likely coming.

item.title: @wallstengine: $GNRC SIGNS UP TO $8B $AMZN DATA CENTER POWER DEAL Generac has entered into a long-term agreement t...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GNRC SIGNS UP TO $8B $AMZN DATA CENTER POWER DEAL
Generac has entered into a long-term agreement to supply backup power generators for Amazon data centers, with aggregate payments under the deal potentially reaching $8 billion.
Initial generator deliveries are expected to total about $2.4 billion across 2027 and 2028.
As part of the agreement, Amazon received warrants to purchase up to 1.69 million Generac shares at $200.93 each. About 308,000 shares vested immediately, while the rest will vest in stages as Amazon’s payments to Generac increase toward the $8B threshold.
The warrants can be exercised through September 2033.
The deal gives Generac a major long-term customer as hyperscalers continue expanding data center capacity and the power infrastructure needed to support it.

item.description:
Today is another reminder of just how fast things can change.
Just 9 months ago, markets were pricing in 3 rate cuts in 2026 and we had $60 oil prices.
Today, a new Fed rate hike cycle has begun, oil prices are above $100, and diesel prices are at record highs.
The market and the Fed are in agreement, lower rates are not coming as long as the current energy crisis continues.
There simply is no scenario where rate cuts are warranted with $100+ oil prices and 3.5%+ inflation, aside from an economic depression.
Luckily, we are also in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in history, and the AI boom continues to provide substantial support for the S&P 500.
Without the AI Revolution, markets would be in a much darker position right now.
On the flip side, a resolution to the current energy crisis opens for the S&P 500 to rise well above 8,000.
For now, a long and bumpy road appears to be ahead as the Fed continues its 60-straight-month battle against inflation.
"Higher for longer" has returned.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
SUMMARY OF FED CHAIR WARSH'S STATEMENT (9/16/26):
1. Warsh says the decision to hike rates comes at a time when the economy is "strengthening"
2. Warsh says he is "hard-pressed to call financial conditions restrictive"
3. The view that conditions are not restrictive was "widely shared by the FOMC"

5. Warsh says he did not submit a dot for the Fed's dot-plot
6. The Fed "must be confident that inflation is moving to our 2% objective"
The Fed is highly committed to obtaining 2% inflation.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The Fed made a very clear statement today. Not only did they hike interest rates, but it was a 12-0...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The Fed made a very clear statement today.
Not only did they hike interest rates, but it was a 12-0 unanimous decision.
This marks the first unanimous Fed decision since May 2025, amid calls from President Trump to cut rates.
And, the Fed concluded their policy statement by saying, "The Committee will deliver price stability," making it clear that inflation is their top priority.
The question now becomes: How does President Trump respond?
12 days ago, President Trump said he would "stop trading" with 50+ US trade partners if the Fed does not cut rates.
Today, the Fed not only avoided cutting rates, they hiked them.
Clearly, the divide between the White House and the Fed is widening, even with Jerome Powell out.
More to come.
item.content:encoded:
The Fed made a very clear statement today.

Not only did they hike interest rates, but it was a 12-0 unanimous decision.

This marks the first unanimous Fed decision since May 2025, amid calls from President Trump to cut rates.

And, the Fed concluded their policy statement by saying, "The Committee will deliver price stability," making it clear that inflation is their top priority.

The question now becomes: How does President Trump respond?

12 days ago, President Trump said he would "stop trading" with 50+ US trade partners if the Fed does not cut rates.

Today, the Fed not only avoided cutting rates, they hiked them.

Clearly, the divide between the White House and the Fed is widening, even with Jerome Powell out.

More to come.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Fed September rate decision, key takeaways: 1. The Fed raised the federal funds target range 25bp t...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Fed September rate decision, key takeaways:
1. The Fed raised the federal funds target range 25bp to 3.75%-4%, its first hike in three years and in line with market expectations.
2. The vote was unanimous at 12-0. July's decision drew three dissents at 9-3.
3. The dot plot median showed two 25bp hikes in 2026 and none in 2027, hawkish versus June, which had one 2026 hike and a 2027 cut, but dovish versus pre-meeting market pricing for four cumulative hikes by June 2027.
4. The Fed raised its GDP forecasts for 2026 and 2027 and lifted its 2026 headline and core inflation forecasts. It cut unemployment forecasts for 2026 through 2028.
5. The statement said today's move will support a "timelier" return to the 2% goal.
item.content:encoded:
Fed September rate decision, key takeaways:

1. The Fed raised the federal funds target range 25bp to 3.75%-4%, its first hike in three years and in line with market expectations.

3. The dot plot median showed two 25bp hikes in 2026 and none in 2027, hawkish versus June, which had one 2026 hike and a 2027 cut, but dovish versus pre-meeting market pricing for four cumulative hikes by June 2027.

4. The Fed raised its GDP forecasts for 2026 and 2027 and lifted its 2026 headline and core inflation forecasts. It cut unemployment forecasts for 2026 through 2028.

5. The statement said today's move will support a "timelier" return to the 2% goal.

item.title: @Hedgeye: McCullough: Nobody's Talking About the Euro Breakup Trade 🔊 In their most recent Real Conversation...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: Nobody's Talking About the Euro Breakup Trade
🔊
In their most recent Real Conversation, @Mike_Taylor1972 and @KeithMcCullough lay out a demographic and political setup for Europe that ends in a currency breakup.
Strip out recent immigrants and Europe's working-age population, ages 18 to 65, falls about 7% over the next decade.
Taylor's point, unit volumes for coffee cups, t-shirts, gasoline, cars, tires, windows, and houses fall 7% over the decade, and levered businesses across the continent can't pay their coupons on shrinking demand.
The only lever left is the printing press, because Europe has run out of room on the long end.
Then the politics.
Opposition parties are polling well ahead of the establishment into next year's elections, and Taylor's base case is a protest party taking France back to the franc.
"We are designing a world where we are able to outrun the European Union," he says.
When Europe breaks, US paper looks clean and the long end of the US yield curve fixes itself.
Watch the full Real Conversation with Mike Taylor and Keith McCullough: https://app.hedgeye.com/insights/187027-real-conversation-the-ai-bubble-and-the-market-risks-ahead?type=%2C

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
A federal judge in Texas ordered Elon Musk's X Corp and SpaceXAI to file their settlement with $AAPL by Thursday, after co-defendant OpenAI argued it needs the terms to fight Musk's remaining claims, per Reuters.
X dropped Apple from its antitrust suit this week without disclosing terms while keeping its case against OpenAI alive. OpenAI's lawyers say the deal could undercut any bid by X to extract money from OpenAI.
The suit alleges Apple broke antitrust law by exclusively integrating ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence; Apple says the deal was never exclusive.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are no longer hedging against a tech stock crash. The average 1-month put-to-call skew of...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are no longer hedging against a tech stock crash.
The average 1-month put-to-call skew of the Nasdaq 100 index is down to 0 points, its 4th-lowest reading over the last 20 years.
This measures how much more investors are paying for downside protection through put options than for upside exposure through call options, with the current reading indicating historically low demand for Nasdaq put options.
This figure has dropped -0.25 points since March 2026, one of the largest 6-month declines on record.
By comparison, the long-term average of this metric is 0.11 points.
Meanwhile, the cost of options used to bet on or protect against large moves in the average Nasdaq 100 stock fell sharply last week, with 1-month implied volatility dropping -17 percentage points, to ~40%.
Investors are extremely bullish on tech.

BREAKING: Hedge funds purchased the most US Information Technology and Communication Services sector equities over the 2 weeks ending September 10th since June 2025.
The greatest demand was recorded in Semiconductor and Semiconductor Equipment, Interactive Media and Services, and Information Technology Services.
This was driven particularly by long purchases, while shorting activity was subdued.
As a result, both sectors were the most bought among all sectors for 2 consecutive weeks.

Hedge funds are loading up on tech stocks.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AAPL WEIGHS RETURN TO SERVER MARKET WITH $NVDA TECH
Apple is reportedly developing an AI-focused enterprise server using its own M-series chips and has discussed using Nvidia NVLink Fusion networking technology to connect them, according to The Information.
The proposed systems would use either two or four M8 Ultra chips and target AI developers, enterprises and governments, with a focus on running AI inference on private infrastructure.
The product is currently aimed for 2029, though plans could still change or be canceled.
The move follows a surge in demand for Mac mini and Mac Studio systems from AI developers, with Mac revenue up nearly 29% last quarter to $10.4B.
If launched, it would mark Apple’s return to the server market for the first time since discontinuing Xserve in 2011.
Source: The Information

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's officially Fed day. Markets now see a 93% chance that the Fed will announce its first rate hik...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's officially Fed day.
Markets now see a 93% chance that the Fed will announce its first rate hike since July 2023 today.
In data going back to 2008, whenever expectations of a hike have been this high, the Fed has invariably delivered one.
If the Fed decided to leave interest rates unchanged today, it would mark the biggest dovish surprise at a scheduled policy meeting since 1994.
However, it's a particularly unusual time right now.
Fed Chair Warsh was appointed by President Trump just months ago with the expectation that he would CUT rates.
Now, markets expect Warsh's first change to the Fed Funds Rate to be a hike.
We expect a highly eventful day.
Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real time analysis as the Fed decision is announced.

item.title: @wallstengine: $CRWV DEPLOYS MULTI-RACK $NVDA VERA RUBIN NVL72 CLUSTER CoreWeave says it has connected hundreds of...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$CRWV DEPLOYS MULTI-RACK $NVDA VERA RUBIN NVL72 CLUSTER
CoreWeave says it has connected hundreds of Nvidia Rubin GPUs into a single scale-out cluster on CoreWeave Cloud, targeting large agentic AI workloads.
Each Vera Rubin NVL72 rack combines 72 Rubin GPUs with 36 Vera CPUs, while the multi-rack setup uses Nvidia Spectrum-X networking to link racks together. Each Rubin GPU gets 1.6 Tb/s of network connectivity, with the fabric designed to scale to roughly 128,000 GPUs per rail.
CoreWeave also rolled out cross-region write acceleration and a new lower-cost Archive tier for AI Object Storage. Its LOTA storage accelerator claims up to 7 GB/s throughput per GPU and an 8x reduction in read latency versus traditional storage clusters.
CoreWeave says it was the first AI cloud provider to validate and deploy a single-rack Vera Rubin NVL72 before expanding to multi-rack deployments.

item.description:
BREAKING: In a major shift, the European Union has officially proposed making Canada the bloc’s first-ever “associate member.”
Details include:
1. European Commission President von der Leyen said Europe needs to "tighten its cooperation with like-minded democracies"
2. von der Leyen also says this would retain the continent’s sovereignty and tackle threats from “an openly hostile world”
3. The move comes just days after President Trump imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods
4. Canada's Prime Minister Carney has confirmed that there are also discussions on certain types of mutual visa-free travel and work arrangements
The trade war and AI are redefining global power dynamics.

item.title: @wallstengine: IBM-BACKED ANDERON SECURES $1B CHIPS AWARD FOR U.S. QUANTUM FOUNDRY Anderon, an $IBM company, final...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
IBM-BACKED ANDERON SECURES $1B CHIPS AWARD FOR U.S. QUANTUM FOUNDRY
Anderon, an $IBM company, finalized a $1 billion CHIPS and Science Act award with the U.S. Department of Commerce to expand R&D and manufacturing capabilities for quantum wafers in Albany, New York.
The company operates a 300mm pure-play quantum wafer foundry and is also backed by an additional $1 billion investment from IBM, bringing total announced government and IBM support around the project to $2 billion.
Anderon will manufacture specialized wafers used for superconducting qubit arrays, quantum input/output signaling and readout components, with plans to support additional quantum computing architectures over time.
The company says its first quantum wafers are already moving through the Albany facility, an early step toward taking quantum chip manufacturing from research-scale processes to commercial-grade production.
For IBM, the foundry is intended to provide the manufacturing capacity needed to support its quantum computing roadmap while also offering wafer fabrication services to other companies across the quantum ecosystem.

The company operates a 300mm pure-play quantum wafer foundry and is also backed by an additional $1 billion investment from IBM, bringing total announced government and IBM support around the project to $2 billion.

Anderon will manufacture specialized wafers used for superconducting qubit arrays, quantum input/output signaling and readout components, with plans to support additional quantum computing architectures over time.

The company says its first quantum wafers are already moving through the Albany facility, an early step toward taking quantum chip manufacturing from research-scale processes to commercial-grade production.

For IBM, the foundry is intended to provide the manufacturing capacity needed to support its quantum computing roadmap while also offering wafer fabrication services to other companies across the quantum ecosystem.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Chinese gold ETFs added +11 tonnes of gold in August, marking their 2nd consecutive month...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Chinese gold ETFs added +11 tonnes of gold in August, marking their 2nd consecutive monthly increase.
This brings their total gold holdings up to 293 tonnes, the highest level since April and the 3rd-highest reading on record.
This comes as investor demand surged, following a partial recovery in Chinese gold prices from their March-June declines, while Chinese government bond yields continued to fall.
Year-to-date, Chinese gold ETFs have acquired +45 tonnes of gold, on track for their 2nd-largest annual inflow on record.
Meanwhile, data suggests Chinese investors continued accumulating gold ETFs in early September, as falling bond yields and weak domestic equity markets supported demand for gold.
China’s appetite for gold is surging.

Net long speculative positioning in the Japanese Yen jumped to +10,796 contracts in the week ending September 8th, the highest in 6 months.
This positioning reflects investors such as hedge funds, asset managers, CTAs, and other money managers that take positions based on price trends and macro views rather than hedging needs.
This marks a sharp reversal from net short positioning of -92,227 contracts in the prior week.
By comparison, in the week ending August 2nd, net short positioning peaked at -163,412 contracts.
This comes as investors are increasingly betting on the Bank of Japan hiking rates which could also encourage domestic investors to bring money back home.
Meanwhile, the unwinding of Yen-funded carry trades could provide further support for the currency.
The Japanese Yen is undergoing a major shift in sentiment.

OpenAI has held early talks with investors about another private funding round that could value the company at roughly $1.2T, up from $852B in March.
The discussions were reportedly initiated by investors and are still at an early stage.
OpenAI’s annualized revenue passed $40B last month after jumping about 20% following GPT-5.6, while Sam Altman has said an IPO is unlikely before 2027.
The company raised $122B in March and spent $34B last year.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The 10Y Note Yield has now traded above its 2-year low for 73 consecutive months, the lon...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The 10Y Note Yield has now traded above its 2-year low for 73 consecutive months, the longest such streak since 1967.
1967 marked the middle of a secular uptrend in the 10Y Note Yield, which ended in the early-1980s.
The streak is now on track to reach 74 consecutive months in September, which would mark the 3rd-longest stretch in history.
Meanwhile, since the September 2022 breakout, the 10Y Note Yield has averaged 4.17%.
This is double the 2.06% average recorded over the previous 10 years.
"Higher for longer" is back.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US long-term unemployment is at crisis levels: The number of Americans unemployed for 27+ weeks sur...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US long-term unemployment is at crisis levels:
The number of Americans unemployed for 27+ weeks surged +155,000 in August, to 1.93 million, the 4th-highest reading since December 2021.
As a % of total unemployment, this metric rose +1.5 percentage points last month, to 27.0%, the 3rd-highest since December 2021.
Long-term unemployment has now increased for more than 3 years.
This figure is now higher than in every recession except the 2008 Financial Crisis and the 2020 Pandemic.
By comparison, during the current economic cycle, this percentage bottomed at 17.8% in February 2023.
The labor market continues to appear weak beneath the surface.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Customer intelligence is becoming a huge market. The customer intelligence market includes the soft...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Customer intelligence is becoming a huge market.
The customer intelligence market includes the software, tools, and services businesses use to collect and analyze consumer data.
In 2023, this market was worth $2.5 billion.
By 2030, this market is expected to exceed $13 billion.
This would mark a +28.3% CAGR from 2024 to 2030, particularly driven by AI adoption.
The reality is that AI has dramatically increased both the amount of consumer data companies can process and the value they can extract from it.
AI is turning data into actionable intelligence at an unprecedented scale.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Markets are bracing for a rate hike. So, how do US stocks usually behave following the first hike o...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Markets are bracing for a rate hike.
So, how do US stocks usually behave following the first hike of a Fed tightening cycle?
The S&P 500 has declined by an average of -4.0% over the 6 weeks following the first Fed rate hike of a cycle across 7 such episodes since 1988.
Subsequently, however, stocks recovered all of those losses over the next 5-6 weeks on average.
Then, in the 6 months following the first hike, the S&P 500 returned +4.0% on average.
After 12 months, the S&P 500’s average gain surged to +9.0%, with positive returns occurring in every episode except 2022.
Fed rate hikes have historically been great buying opportunities.

Google introduced two new real-time voice models designed for conversational AI and agentic workflows.
Gemini 3.8 Live is built for scale and lower-cost deployment, while 3.8 Live Extended Thinking adds deeper multi-step reasoning while continuing to speak and narrate progress during longer tasks.
Both models support near real-time visual understanding, automatic switching across 97 languages and background tool/API calls without interrupting the conversation.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA says AI factories are increasingly being measured by how much useful compute they can produce from each megawatt of power.
Nvidia's DSX MaxLPS software can enable Vera Rubin NVL72 deployments to support up to 40% more GPUs and 35% higher token throughput within the same site-power envelope.
In new Lambda testing on Blackwell, 19 nodes ran within a power budget normally sized for 16, increasing token throughput 24% and performance per watt 23%.

NVIDIA and Emerald AI also demonstrated AI infrastructure that can automatically throttle lower-priority workloads when the grid needs power, then restore them as capacity returns.

In other words, the monthly payment on a $500,000 mortgage has gone from ~$3,000 to ~$3,400 in 7 months.
That's an increase of +$400/month or +$4,800/year.
Homeownership is historically unattainable right now.

item.title: @wallstengine: ODYSSEY UNVEILS ODYSSEY-3, A GENERAL-PURPOSE WORLD MODEL FOR PHYSICAL AI Odyssey-3 is a new foundat...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ODYSSEY UNVEILS ODYSSEY-3, A GENERAL-PURPOSE WORLD MODEL FOR PHYSICAL AI
Odyssey-3 is a new foundation world model designed to power robot arms, humanoids, autonomous vehicles, drones, AI agents and even video game systems from the same pretrained model.
The model can learn new physical tasks with relatively little task-specific data. Odyssey says it learned autonomous driving from just 20 hours of simulated driving data, while robot and humanoid policies were trained with only tens of hours of demonstrations.
The idea is to move away from building a separate AI system for every machine and instead use one model with a shared understanding of physics, dynamics and cause-and-effect across different environments.
Odyssey plans to release Odyssey-3 publicly in the coming weeks.

item.title: @wallstengine: RAMP EXPANDS TO UK IN FIRST MAJOR MOVE OUTSIDE NORTH AMERICA Fintech platform Ramp has officially l...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
RAMP EXPANDS TO UK IN FIRST MAJOR MOVE OUTSIDE NORTH AMERICA
Fintech platform Ramp has officially launched in the UK, marking its first major international expansion beyond North America.
Ramp offers corporate cards, bill payments and AI-powered spend management tools. The company was valued at $44 billion after raising $750 million in June and is reportedly in early talks for another funding round at roughly a $60 billion valuation.
The expansion follows Ramp’s acquisition of Stockholm-based Billhop in March, which gave the company regulatory access across the European Economic Area and separate authorization from the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority.
Ramp says AI-related spending across its customers has increased roughly 21x since June 2025, while its heaviest AI spenders have seen costs rise 50% or more roughly every quarter.
The company competes with Brex, American Express, JPMorgan and Citi in corporate spending and financial management.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @wallstengine: AWS, COGNITION SIGN MULTI-YEAR DEVIN DEAL AWS and Cognition are teaming up to push Devin deeper int...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
AWS, COGNITION SIGN MULTI-YEAR DEVIN DEAL
AWS and Cognition are teaming up to push Devin deeper into enterprise software modernization, targeting one of the biggest bottlenecks in large companies: old code, security backlogs and migration work.
Devin will be used to analyze legacy systems, write replacement code, test migrations and run multiple engineering tasks in parallel inside AWS environments.
The interesting part is the productivity claim.
Mercedes-Benz used Devin to analyze more than 200,000 lines of COBOL, cutting an estimated 8-month modernization project to 8 days.
Another automaker used Devin to move a 25,000-line COBOL workflow to AWS Lambda, with an estimated 73% cost reduction.
Devin can also run in single-tenant AWS environments with dedicated VPCs, regional controls and audit logs, which makes the product easier to deploy inside large enterprises with strict security requirements.
This looks like AWS moving beyond simply hosting AI models and starting to integrate autonomous coding agents directly into enterprise migration and infrastructure workflows.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META TO ROLL OUT TWO NEW IN-HOUSE AI CHIPS IN 2027, PLANS 1GW+ OF CUSTOM SILICON CAPACITY Meta pla...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META TO ROLL OUT TWO NEW IN-HOUSE AI CHIPS IN 2027, PLANS 1GW+ OF CUSTOM SILICON CAPACITY
Meta plans to begin deploying its new MTIA 450 chip, code-named Arke, across data centers in the first half of 2027, as it pushes to reduce the cost and energy required to run AI models.
The next-generation MTIA 500, code-named Astrid, is expected to finish design work in roughly a month and enter data centers by the end of 2027. Meta expects Astrid to be deployed even more broadly than Arke.
Meta is working with Broadcom $AVGO on chip design and TSMC on manufacturing.
The company has already committed to more than 1 gigawatt of capacity using its custom chips over a 12-month period and expects deployment to accelerate after that.
Meta received its first 12 Arke chips from TSMC on Sept. 1. Early testing showed performance within 2% to 3% of simulations, and the chips were able to run models from Meta, DeepSeek and Alibaba on the first day.
The chips are designed primarily as general-purpose inference “workhorses,” rather than for the fastest latency-sensitive workloads. Meta says its close coordination between its AI teams and chip designers allows the hardware to deliver better performance per watt and per dollar for its own workloads than current NVIDIA systems.
Meta also canceled a previously planned chip called Olympus, which was intended to handle both AI training and inference, after determining that such a design could cost roughly 30% more. The company is instead concentrating its custom silicon roadmap on lower-cost inference at gigawatt scale.
After Astrid, Meta plans to focus future generations on higher speed and throughput, including using fiber-optic technologies to improve performance.
Source: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
$META TO ROLL OUT TWO NEW IN-HOUSE AI CHIPS IN 2027, PLANS 1GW+ OF CUSTOM SILICON CAPACITY

Meta plans to begin deploying its new MTIA 450 chip, code-named Arke, across data centers in the first half of 2027, as it pushes to reduce the cost and energy required to run AI models.

The next-generation MTIA 500, code-named Astrid, is expected to finish design work in roughly a month and enter data centers by the end of 2027. Meta expects Astrid to be deployed even more broadly than Arke.

Meta is working with Broadcom $AVGO on chip design and TSMC on manufacturing.

The company has already committed to more than 1 gigawatt of capacity using its custom chips over a 12-month period and expects deployment to accelerate after that.

Meta received its first 12 Arke chips from TSMC on Sept. 1. Early testing showed performance within 2% to 3% of simulations, and the chips were able to run models from Meta, DeepSeek and Alibaba on the first day.

The chips are designed primarily as general-purpose inference “workhorses,” rather than for the fastest latency-sensitive workloads. Meta says its close coordination between its AI teams and chip designers allows the hardware to deliver better performance per watt and per dollar for its own workloads than current NVIDIA systems.

Meta also canceled a previously planned chip called Olympus, which was intended to handle both AI training and inference, after determining that such a design could cost roughly 30% more. The company is instead concentrating its custom silicon roadmap on lower-cost inference at gigawatt scale.

After Astrid, Meta plans to focus future generations on higher speed and throughput, including using fiber-optic technologies to improve performance.

Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @Hedgeye: Jet fuel is now over double what it cost a year ago: Fuel is an airline's single largest operating...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Jet fuel is now over double what it cost a year ago:
Fuel is an airline's single largest operating expense, and it's the one cost they can't fully control.
The gap between jet fuel and crude, the jet fuel crack spread, has spiked toward $70 a barrel, more than double the post-Covid average and far above the $14 pre-Covid norm.
For decades, jet fuel tracked crude closely, so airlines could manage fuel risk through oil.
That link has snapped.
Years of shrinking refining capacity, plus tighter rules on middle-distillate fuels since 2020, have left less slack in the system and more exposure to shocks.
And what many don't realize is that diesel drives the whole stream.
Diesel just hit an all-time record $6.27 a gallon, dragging its refining cousin jet fuel up with it, and crude is back above $100/bbl on the escalating attacks in the Middle East.
Airlines' fuel bill is set to jump nearly +40% this year, and industry profits are on track to roughly halve.
Airlines are under pressure.

item.title: @wallstengine: CRUSOE SIGNS MULTIYEAR AI CLOUD DEAL WITH PERPLEXITY Crusoe has signed a multiyear cloud agreement...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CRUSOE SIGNS MULTIYEAR AI CLOUD DEAL WITH PERPLEXITY
Crusoe has signed a multiyear cloud agreement with Perplexity AI, expanding its push to compete with neocloud providers like CoreWeave $CRWV & Nebius $NBIS.
Perplexity will use $NVDA GPUs from Crusoe to train and run AI models, including access to GB300 systems, while Crusoe will manage the infrastructure over its lifecycle.
Financial terms were not disclosed.
As part of the deal, Crusoe will also provide Perplexity Enterprise Max to more than 1,800 employees.
The agreement comes shortly after Crusoe signed a roughly $13B AI cloud deal with Jane Street.
Crusoe says it also has access to NVIDIA’s upcoming Vera Rubin processors.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US consumers aged 40-49 now account for 26.8% of new consumer bankruptcies, their highest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US consumers aged 40-49 now account for 26.8% of new consumer bankruptcies, their highest proportion since Q3 2015 and the largest among all age groups.
At the same time, the 50-59 group represents 23.1%, bringing the combined proportion of Americans aged 40-59 to 49.9%, the largest since Q1 2017.
To put this into perspective, this figure peaked at 54.3% in Q4 2011, following the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Furthermore, those aged 70+ now make up 21.5% of all new consumer bankruptcies, their largest proportion since Q2 2017.
Meanwhile, Americans aged 18-29 now account for only 5.9% of new bankruptcies, their lowest percentage since Q2 2014.
Older Americans are falling behind on their debt.

item.title: @wallstengine: $GOOGL OPENS ANTHROPIC’S CLAUDE TO ENGINEERS COMPANY-WIDE Google is now allowing engineers across t...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL OPENS ANTHROPIC’S CLAUDE TO ENGINEERS COMPANY-WIDE
Google is now allowing engineers across the company to use Anthropic’s Claude for internal coding work, a notable shift from its previous policy of largely restricting employees to Gemini, according to Business Insider.
Employees can access **Anthropic’s Opus 5** model through Antigravity, Google’s internal development platform. Access is subject to per-user quotas and is intended to supplement, not replace, Gemini.
Previously, Claude access was mostly limited to select DeepMind teams and certain high-priority engineering projects, while outside coding tools such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex were generally restricted.
The change comes as competition in AI coding intensifies and engineers push for access to the strongest available models to improve productivity.
Google says Gemini remains its “primary and foundational” model for internal development, while third-party models will be available for specialized use cases.
Google is also a major Anthropic investor and earlier this year announced plans to invest **up to $40B** in the company.
Source: Business Insider

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Global oil demand is declining sharply amid rising prices: The IEA has cut its forecast for 2026 gl...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Global oil demand is declining sharply amid rising prices:
The IEA has cut its forecast for 2026 global oil demand by -940,000 barrels per day, now expecting consumption to fall -2.5 million barrels per day, the largest annual decline since the 2020 pandemic.
This compares with a -1.6 million barrel per day drop expected in August and just a -100,000 barrel per day expected decline in April.
To put this into perspective, in January, the IEA saw oil consumption rising by over +700,000 barrels per day in 2026.
The downgrade comes as the Iran War disrupts oil supplies and forces consumers to adjust to tighter availability, with the biggest impact expected on diesel and other middle distillates such as jet fuel and heating oil.
The negative impact on oil demand this year is expected to be comparable in size to the 4 largest demand shocks over the last 60 years.
Oil demand is collapsing as prices surge.

item.description:
President Trump is now calling the AI safety concerns that were voiced by big tech CEOs this weekend a “hoax.”
He has voiced his opposition to AI safety concerns five times now since Saturday.
This marks the biggest divergence yet between the White House and the leaders building frontier AI.
The reality is that we are now in an AI arms race.
Without an international agreement, compliance with which would arguably be nearly impossible to regulate, no one has an incentive to slow down.
If one party slows down, but the other doesn’t, the former will be left in the dust.
The question now becomes, will big tech CEOs go against Trump on this?
If so, it will have market-moving implications.
This is the era of disruption.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US housing market is officially a buyer's market: There were an estimated +57.9% more home sell...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US housing market is officially a buyer's market:
There were an estimated +57.9% more home sellers than buyers in August, the biggest gap on record.
This is up sharply from +52.1% the month before, which was the 2nd-strongest buyer's market on record.
This comes as the number of active sellers surged +3.9% MoM, or +57,958, to 1,534,918, the most since early 2020,marking the largest monthly increase on record.
At the same time, there were ~972,300 active homebuyers, the 2nd-lowest reading on record.
This brings the gap between active sellers and homebuyers to a massive 562,618.
As a result, 36 of the 49 major US metros are now buyer's markets, led by Nashville, where sellers outnumber buyers by +139%, followed by Miami at +138%, and Houston at +131%.
Historically low affordability is causing buyers to quit.

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: Why the Semis Rally Is More Fragile Than It Looks
🔊
On Monday's edition of The Macro Show, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough explained why the semiconductor rally is more fragile than it looks and why he expects the Fed's next move to backfire.
McCullough's point on the flows, the recent semis rally has been perpetuated by mechanical buying rather than conviction.
As volatility came off the lows last week, volatility-control funds were buying the index, and with semis a heavy index weight, that flow carried the group higher. The risk is that it reverses.
If one-month volatility breaks back above three-month, and CTAs start selling, which the morning's Tier 1 Alpha review suggested had already begun, anyone chasing semis into that flow has a problem.
The macro backdrop is a Fed hike landing right at the top of the Risk Range™.
The catalyst for the next cut will be the hike itself, which inverts and, in his words, "pancakes" the yield curve, exactly what is already happening. We expect the outcome to be messy.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AAPL LAUNCHES NEW SIRI AI WITH PERSONAL CONTEXT Apple has begun rolling out Siri AI in beta with i...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AAPL LAUNCHES NEW SIRI AI WITH PERSONAL CONTEXT
Apple has begun rolling out Siri AI in beta with iOS 27, adding personal context across messages, emails and photos, along with onscreen awareness and systemwide app actions.
The new Siri can find information across a user’s device, understand what is on screen, draft emails, add calendar events and take actions across supported apps.
Apple says the new Apple Intelligence architecture uses its own foundation models built in collaboration with Google and Gemini, with processing split between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute.
Siri AI will initially support English on Apple Intelligence-capable devices, including the iPhone 15 Pro and newer.
It will not initially be available in the EU on iOS, iPadOS or watchOS, and Siri AI and the new Apple Intelligence features will not be available in China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.
Apple also says some server-side AI features will have daily usage limits, with expanded access available for a fee in the future.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA EXPANDS PINTEREST AI PARTNERSHIP, DELIVERS 85X FASTER RESPONSE STARTUP Pinterest has expanded...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA EXPANDS PINTEREST AI PARTNERSHIP, DELIVERS 85X FASTER RESPONSE STARTUP
Pinterest has expanded its partnership with Nvidia to build a shared multimodal AI infrastructure for visual search, recommendations, safety and its Pinterest Assistant.
The system combines NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, NVIDIA Dynamo, open-source models and Pinterest’s own visual embeddings.
In benchmark testing, Pinterest saw:
• ~85x faster response startup • 7.3x faster overall latency • 25x more visual context per request for Pinterest Assistant
The infrastructure is designed to turn Pinterest’s 80B+ monthly searches into signals for AI-powered discovery and shopping, while avoiding the need to repeatedly process raw images.
The partnership builds on nearly five years of work and more than 14,000 NVIDIA GPUs, with the same platform now supporting ranking, OCR, safety, signal generation and future vision-language model applications.

item.title: @wallstengine: PERPLEXITY BRINGS ITS LOCAL AI AGENT TO WINDOWS PCs POWERED BY $NVDA RTX Perplexity has launched Po...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
PERPLEXITY BRINGS ITS LOCAL AI AGENT TO WINDOWS PCs POWERED BY $NVDA RTX
Perplexity has launched Portable Computer for Windows, bringing its local-first AI agent to compatible NVIDIA GeForce RTX PCs and RTX PRO workstations.
The agent can plan and execute multi-step workflows directly on the PC, analyze local files and use connected apps while keeping sensitive data on-device.
Work completed locally also does not consume Perplexity Computer credits.
Portable Computer ships with a locally optimized model such as Qwen 3.8 27B and can automatically determine when a task needs stronger cloud reasoning, asking for permission before sending any data off-device.
It also supports connectors for Outlook, OneDrive, Word, Google Drive, Gmail, Slack and GitHub, allowing users to run workflows across existing files and apps.
The Windows release requires an NVIDIA RTX GPU with 24GB or more of VRAM and expands on existing support for DGX Spark and Linux RTX systems.

The agent can plan and execute multi-step workflows directly on the PC, analyze local files and use connected apps while keeping sensitive data on-device.

Work completed locally also does not consume Perplexity Computer credits.

Portable Computer ships with a locally optimized model such as Qwen 3.8 27B and can automatically determine when a task needs stronger cloud reasoning, asking for permission before sending any data off-device.

It also supports connectors for Outlook, OneDrive, Word, Google Drive, Gmail, Slack and GitHub, allowing users to run workflows across existing files and apps.

The Windows release requires an NVIDIA RTX GPU with 24GB or more of VRAM and expands on existing support for DGX Spark and Linux RTX systems.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA EXPANDS CUDA-Q FOR FAULT-TOLERANT QUANTUM COMPUTING Nvidia has launched CUDA-Q Logical, a new...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA EXPANDS CUDA-Q FOR FAULT-TOLERANT QUANTUM COMPUTING
Nvidia has launched CUDA-Q Logical, a new open-source layer designed to help researchers build and test fault-tolerant quantum systems by jointly optimizing algorithms, error correction and hardware requirements.
Fermilab says the platform cut one architecture-development workflow from roughly five months to three weeks, a 7x speedup.
Iceberg Quantum and Diraq also used it to model 1,000 logical qubits using 150,000 physical qubits, about 10x fewer than Diraq’s previous estimates. These are simulated resource estimates, not operating logical qubits today.
Nvidia is also adding QUOPS, a hardware-agnostic benchmark developed by Sandia National Laboratories to compare progress toward utility-scale quantum computing across different platforms.
CUDA-Q Logical is already being used by Fermilab, Sandia, Infleqtion, IQM, QCDesign and Quantum Motion.
The broader strategy is hardware-agnostic: Nvidia is building the software, GPU and interconnect layer that can sit between different quantum processors and classical supercomputers, regardless of which qubit architecture ultimately wins.

Fermilab says the platform cut one architecture-development workflow from roughly five months to three weeks, a 7x speedup.

Iceberg Quantum and Diraq also used it to model 1,000 logical qubits using 150,000 physical qubits, about 10x fewer than Diraq’s previous estimates. These are simulated resource estimates, not operating logical qubits today.

Nvidia is also adding QUOPS, a hardware-agnostic benchmark developed by Sandia National Laboratories to compare progress toward utility-scale quantum computing across different platforms.

CUDA-Q Logical is already being used by Fermilab, Sandia, Infleqtion, IQM, QCDesign and Quantum Motion.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Microsoft, $MSFT, announces "limits" for future AI models through a new code of conduct a...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Microsoft, $MSFT, announces "limits" for future AI models through a new code of conduct after recent discussion around AI safety.
Details include:
1. Under the new code of conduct, Microsoft's models are subject to certain limitations
2. Their models must not entertain requests on weapons manufacturing, assist with the procurement of dangerous substances, encourage unhealthy eating, or produce violent or sexually explicit content
3. Models from Microsoft AI must adhere to people’s objectives and "steer clear of creating their own goals"
4. Microsoft is also planning rules to prevent a cyberattack similar to the one carried out on startup Hugging Face
The AI safety discussion is shifting the industry.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US deficit is now up to $1.97 trillion in the first 11 months of FY2026, the 4th-larg...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US deficit is now up to $1.97 trillion in the first 11 months of FY2026, the 4th-largest deficit at this point in the fiscal year in history.
This is already higher than the full-year FY2025 deficit of $1.78 trillion.
In August, the US Treasury's budget deficit technically fell -$178 billion YoY, or -51%, to $167 billion.
This comes as government outlays dropped -$162 billion YoY, to $527 billion, but the decline was largely due to a calendar shift, as August 1st fell on a Saturday, pushing Medicare and Social Security payments normally made on the first of the month into July.
However, adjusting for these payments, which account for some of the largest federal outlays, the monthly deficit rose +$7 billion YoY, to $248 billion, according to the US Treasury.
The US is on an unsustainable fiscal path.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Buckle up for the week of the year. 9 days ago, President Trump threatened to "stop trading" with a...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Buckle up for the week of the year.
9 days ago, President Trump threatened to "stop trading" with all countries that the US has a trade deficit with if the Fed does not CUT rates.
On Wednesday, the Fed will release their September interest rate decision.
Currently, markets believe the Fed will HIKE rates on Wednesday.
In other words, the market now expects Fed Chair Warsh to make the exact opposite policy decision that President Trump wants, just 3 months after he was appointed.
If the market is correct and President Trump follows through on his threat, global trade is about to take a major turn.
This move would effectively cut off trade with ~50% of all US trading partners, including Mexico, China, Taiwan, Germany, Japan, South Korea, Canada, and India.
Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter to receive real time analysis as the week progresses.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It seems most people don't understand how severe the energy situation is right now in the Middle Ea...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It seems most people don't understand how severe the energy situation is right now in the Middle East.
As of Friday, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has officially been shut down after recent attacks, putting -4 million barrels of daily oil exports at risk.
Meanwhile, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait is now at risk of being shut down, threatening up to -9 million barrels of daily oil supply.
All while the Strait of Hormuz is operating at ~20% of its pre-Iran War capacity, removing -15 million barrels of daily oil flows.
Combined, this represents nearly ~30 MILLION barrels per day of oil flows that are either offline or at risk.
Even after accounting for some overlap between these routes, the scale of the potential disruption is enormous relative to the ~100 million barrel per day global oil market.
This is one of the most severe energy supply situations in modern history.

Amazon $AMZN, Alphabet $GOOGL, Microsoft $MSFT and Meta $META have sold over $200 billion of bonds so far in 2026, a record that more than doubles last year's $78 billion.
The pace has accelerated sharply from the prior decade, when the four rarely issued more than $30 billion combined in a full year.
The debt is funding a surge in AI infrastructure spending, from data centers to chips, and 2026 is only year to date.
Combined capex guidance for the four now runs near $700 billion this year.
Cash flow no longer covers it, Amazon's spending ran to 102% of operating cash flow over the trailing year.
The buildout now runs near 2% of U.S. GDP, and by some estimates accounts for about a third of this year's growth.
The debt is how they're funding it.
item.content:encoded:
Hyperscaler debt is soaring:

Amazon $AMZN, Alphabet $GOOGL, Microsoft $MSFT and Meta $META have sold over $200 billion of bonds so far in 2026, a record that more than doubles last year's $78 billion.

The pace has accelerated sharply from the prior decade, when the four rarely issued more than $30 billion combined in a full year.

The debt is funding a surge in AI infrastructure spending, from data centers to chips, and 2026 is only year to date.

Combined capex guidance for the four now runs near $700 billion this year.

Cash flow no longer covers it, Amazon's spending ran to 102% of operating cash flow over the trailing year.

The buildout now runs near 2% of U.S. GDP, and by some estimates accounts for about a third of this year's growth.

The debt is how they're funding it.
